_comment: The cross-language node-registry parity fixture ( Task 3, extended by Task 5 with the five summarization-palette node types, by Task 3 with the eight STT-palette node types — stt.phiHop is implemented:false, a documented placeholder pending and by Task 9 with the consultation palette. The consultation palette now carries ALL THIRTEEN node types of 's node table: shipped three (consentGate, phiHop, hitlGate) and left ten specified-but-unwired, which made the palette unbuildable because DRAFT_CONSULTATION_RULE_SET names nine node types by key; the remaining ten interpreter wrappers were added later over the compile targets palette-contract.md had already verified. consultation.hitlGate remains implemented:false, a documented placeholder pending the interpreter's own durable-wait extension (Phase B), so compile() still refuses any graph containing it. Asserted from BOTH packages/workflow-contract/src/__tests__/node-registry-parity.test.ts (TS) and apps/harness/src/harness/tests/unit/temporal/interpreter/test_node_registry_parity.py (Python) — see packages/workflow-contract/src/node-registry.ts's module docstring for why the two sides check against this file instead of against each other. Also carries the two palette-agnostic GRAPH BOUNDARY MARKERS `core.start`/`core.end` (TS class `boundary`): the palette-independent structural rules WF-S-002/003/004/007 are written against these literal node types, so until they were registered no graph in any palette could validate — the platform's own seeded summarization graph scored 17 errors against its own validator. They execute nothing but are `implemented: true` because compile() refuses any graph containing an unimplemented type. `entries` sorted by `key`. Only fields BOTH registries carry today are listed here; `classes`/`paletteKey` (TS-only) and `kind` (Python-only) are intentionally excluded. Extended by with R3's three missing capabilities — consultation.realtimeSummary, consultation.suggestions and consultation.proposeCorrections — which verified had no node, activity or sensor anywhere. realtimeSummary is externalWrite:true because it publishes to the live consultation feed (so a sandboxed run skips it); suggestions and proposeCorrections are externalWrite:false because both are PROPOSAL surfaces that write nothing — proposeCorrections in particular must never be the thing that edits clinical text. Extended by OD-15 (option A) with `outputKeys`: the ONE port field that is deliberately SHARED rather than TS-only. A port NAME is an authoring handle (`out`, `entities`, `verdict`) — what the canvas draws and what a graph edge's fromPort/toPort names — but the interpreter threads values by reading a KEY out of the producing activity's own NodeActivityResult.output dict, and no activity has ever emitted a key called "out". Before OD-15 the only bridge was the interpreter's whole-object fallback, which is exactly the untyped bundle the port vocabulary exists to abolish. `outputKeys` maps EVERY declared output port name to the key it carries, or to null for a `control` port, which carries no payload at all — that null is what lets _resolve_bound_inputs tell a legitimate ordering edge apart from an edge naming a port that does not exist (the latter raises). Asserted from BOTH sides exactly like every other field here; adding it to one language's projection without the other is a failing test, not a silent drift. Extended by with the ENDPOINT STAGE's three node types — session.timeout, summary.finalize and feedback.capture — the ordered sequence that runs before a consultation session closes. All three are trigger:'on-end', lane:'durable' and therefore idempotent (TS-only fields; the durable-lane idempotency rule is enforced by nodeDescriptorContractProblems, not by this fixture). All three are externalWrite:true: session.timeout stamps the consultation's endpoint disposition, summary.finalize LOCKS every document of the consultation (DD-3, not just the SOAP note), and feedback.capture promotes an ACCEPTED advisory transcript correction over the raw channel (DD-8 — the only path that can; consultation.proposeCorrections stays externalWrite:false and never applies anything). Their outputKeys carry the control port only: each one's product is a state change, not a value, exactly like output.deliver. Extended by lane A with the TARGET CATALOGUE (DD-6/DD-9) — nine agent.* node types — and the three guard.* node types of DD-7, plus a SECOND shared field, `lane`. Every agent.*/guard.* entry is a thin DELEGATION to an engine already registered above (see apps/harness/src/harness/temporal/interpreter/nodes/agent_catalogue.py and nodes/guards.py for the mapping), so there are two names and one implementation rather than a second behaviour to keep in step; they are registered alongside the pipeline keys rather than instead of them, because a node type is a contract with every saved tenant graph and both committed seeds name the pipeline keys. `lane` is shared for the same reason `outputKeys` is — it changes what the interpreter DOES: a `realtime` node belongs to s live executor, so _dispatch_node SKIPS it with reason="realtime_lane" and exactly one runtime ever executes a given node. Before this, descriptor.lane said "durable" on all 36 entries while REALTIME_NODE_TYPES (a hand-kept set in the applications layer) said otherwise for three of them, and the durable interpreter read neither — which for consultation.realtimeSummary (externalWrite:true) meant two engines could write one consultation s document. The three flipped entries lose nothing that was working: in the durable lane consultation.captureBinding emits no transcript, so extractEntities and realtimeSummary already degraded on no_bound_text every run. Extended by Lane N with `agent.important_findings` — the ONE catalogue entry that is not a delegation, because the capability it names did not exist in any form (§14a: "important information highlighted — DOES NOT EXIST"; there was no red-flag, critical-value, allergy-alert or severity layer anywhere). It is `lane: 'realtime'` because the owner's bar is findings surfaced DURING a live session, which no `on-end` durable node can meet, and because the highlight path it publishes onto is the realtime lane's own entity re-anchoring; the durable interpreter therefore SKIPS it with reason="realtime_lane" exactly as it does `agent.grammar`. `externalWrite: true` mirrors `agent.ner`: its findings reach the live consultation feed and the persisted flush snapshot through the same projection, so claiming otherwise would be a false safety claim. `outputKeys.out` is `findings` and not `entities` deliberately — the PRIMITIVE is `entities` so findings ride the existing highlight path, while a distinct runtime KEY is what lets a consumer tell a tenant-declared important finding apart from an NER entity instead of merging two different claims into one highlight set. `guard.groundedness` gained two OPTIONAL INPUT ports in the same lane (the redacted transcript and the highlighted findings the owner says grounding evaluates) and is deliberately ABSENT from this diff: only OUTPUT keys are mirrored here, so an additive input is TS-side only. Amended by TASK-867 (TASK-861 step 10): the `stt` palette is RETIRED — all eight `stt.*` entries are now `implemented: false`, so compile() refuses any stt graph. They stay in this fixture for the deprecation window, but ONLY the TypeScript side carries them: registry.py has NO spec for an `implemented: false` entry (a NodeSpec cannot exist without a registered activity callable, and the interpreter skips a missing spec exactly as it skips an unimplemented one), and the worker serves no `interpreter.stt_*` activity — `nodes/stt_placeholder.py` was deleted. test_node_registry_parity.py therefore matches the `implemented: true` entries exactly and asserts the `implemented: false` ones are absent. Extended by TASK-882 with the two endpoint stages that had no node type — livedoc.stop (externalWrite:true, it closes a real live session) and harness.finalize (externalWrite:false — inside an interpreter run the graph IS the document workflow, so the node is an ordering marker; the loop, not the activity, starts the child). With them the whole endpoint stage is declarable on a graph, which retired the consultation.endpoint.actions setting. Extended by TASK-882 with agent.dna_style — the DNA writing-style gate migrated out of the retired PipelinePolicy cascade: the tenant gate is the node's presence (read by the gateway at prompt assembly), the doctor's opt-out is a UserSettings preference, and inside an interpreter run the node is an ordering marker (externalWrite:false).
